documents.title: Ad hoc Subcommittee on Artificial Intelligence (AI) Running Report, Winter 2024
tiers: Prohibit AI in the class (sample syllabus statement)
Permit AI on conditions: undergraduate classes
Permit AI on conditions: graduate classes
documents.summary: A 2024 Academic Senate ad hoc subcommittee report on AI. It recommends that each instructor decide AI use and state it in the syllabus, offers three sample statements (prohibit, permit for undergraduates, permit for graduates), and covers privacy, equity, integrity education, HR, admissions, IT and advising.
documents.stance_why: The report sets no university rule on AI in classes; it says 'Faculty need to decide whether AI can be used' and that 'The inclusion of such statements is the instructor's decision', then offers sample statements for prohibiting or conditionally permitting AI. That is delegation with tiers.

documents.title: Student Code of Conduct revision resolution (Section 2.3 Cheating includes AI)
documents.summary: A December 2024 Academic Senate resolution revising Section 2.3 of the Student Code of Conduct. It adds the use of AI tools in coursework to the definition of cheating unless the instructor authorized it in advance and it was cited.
documents.stance_why: Section 2.3 defines cheating to include 'using artificial intelligence (AI) tools/systems in academic coursework, except where such use has been authorized in advance by the instructor and disclosed'. AI is banned unless explicitly permitted, which is restrict.

units.why: The resolution states 'AI usage may lead to academic misconduct, it is necessary to amend the definitions', the reason for the change (P36).
